name: Elewana The Manor at Ngorongoro
positioning: Cape Dutch-style manor house and cottages within an Arabica coffee estate in the hills south of the Ngorongoro Crater
best_for: Safari travelers who want a gracious base for visiting Ngorongoro Crater
Travelers who want privacy, garden views and old-world Afro-European style
Families, who can stay in the family cottage

facts.text: The Manor sits on the green, rolling hills south of the Ngorongoro Crater, reached by crossing the Rift Valley.
The Manor is located adjacent to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, in north west Tanzania.
The Manor stands within a 1500-acre Arabica coffee estate.
The Manor is reminiscent of an elegant up-country farm home in the Cape Dutch style of architecture.
The lodge blends East African hospitality with old-world Afro-European architecture and decor.
Accommodation is in cottages around a main Manor House, including a family cottage.
Each cottage is positioned to maximise views of the adjacent verdant hills while keeping intimacy and privacy.
The Manor has gardens set among coffee-bush laden hills.
Ngorongoro Crater, a short distance away, is an extinct volcano with an 18-kilometre-wide crater floor that is home to an abundant and unique ecosystem.
The Manor has its own restaurant, where guests dine after a day at the Crater.

highlights.text: The Manor stands within a 1500-acre Arabica coffee estate, with gardens set among coffee-bush laden hills.
The architecture recalls an elegant up-country farm home in the Cape Dutch style, blending East African hospitality with old-world Afro-European decor.
Each cottage is positioned to maximise views of the adjacent verdant hills while keeping intimacy and privacy.
The Manor is adjacent to the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a short distance from the Ngorongoro Crater.

considerations.text: The Manor is in the hills south of the Ngorongoro Crater, not on the crater itself; the Crater is a short distance away.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires advance planning for access.
WhataHotel notes the high-altitude setting may affect some guests.
